newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Airlines union to call for strike.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Airlines union to call for strike.

text.p: Turkey's Hava-Is labour union, which represents 7,758 workers of the national carrier Turkish Airlines (THY), said it would call for a strike following a three-month deadlock in pay talks.

"The (15-day) negotiation period under an official arbitrator ended on March 25 without an agreement, therefore we will on the second week of April call for a strike," executive board of Hava-Is said in a statement.
The union has demanded pay rises averaging 150 percent for ground personnel and 70 percent for flight personnel for the first six-month period of a two-year contract from January 1, 1997.
It has also demanded inflation plus eight-percentage point rises for each six-month period to follow. Annual inflation in Turkey is currently about 77 percent.
A union official said the THY's offer for the first six months was an average 55 percent.
About 1,400 out of the union's 7,758 members are flight personnel.
